dial.summary: BTC.D holding at 58.9% and open interest climbing to 653,000 BTC ($56.2B) signals sustained spot-led accumulation — macro headwinds (real yields 2.88%, DXY 102.17) persist but are stable, the 2s10s curve steepened to +0.47%, stablecoin dominance eased to 10.5% releasing $300B+ in sidelined capital; with funding rates at only 10% annualized (well below overheating), BTC accumulation continues ahead of September CPI (Oct 14) and the October 27–28 FOMC.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.6T based on August 2026 data (latest available, confirmed Oct 6); component breakdown: US $23.3T, China $53.1T, Eurozone $19.1T, Japan $8.1T; September G4 M2 not yet available (6–8 week reporting lag); 4-week trend flat: no confirmed September G4 data, 3-month growth rate through August +1.17% (normal pace); YoY still meaningfully positive (not contracting); status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; ISM Prices at 77.9% and elevated CPI present a stagflation signal complicating the liquidity expansion narrative; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5%, released October 1 (confirmed via ISM PR Newswire) — ninth consecutive month of manufacturing expansion; 4-week trend flat: August 54.6% → September 54.5% = −0.1pp, within the flat threshold; New Orders Index 55.3% (bullish forward signal); Production Index 56.7%; Prices Index 77.9% (highest since mid-2021, a leading CPI upside signal); status neutral (above 50 but flat; supportive requires above 50 AND rising on 4-week basis); next ISM Manufacturing release November 3, 2026.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 102.17 on October 6, 2026 (up 0.06% from the Oct 5 close of 102.24); 4-week trend up: ~99.9 (Sep 5) → 102.17 (Oct 6) = +2.3% over 30 days, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind (above 100 threshold); DXY near 2-month high reflecting safe-haven demand and persistent USD structural bid; 10Y yield at 5.29%; a sustained close below 100 required to return to neutral status; October 14 CPI is the next major DXY repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.88% as of October 1, 2026 (latest Fed H.15); breakeven inflation rate ~2.28% (stagflation premium building with ISM Prices at 77.9%); 4-week trend up: ~2.50% (Sep 3) → 2.88% (Oct 1) = +38bps over 30 days; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral; October 14 CPI is the next key real yield repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 5, 2026: 10Y Treasury at 5.29%, 2Y at 4.82% → 2s10s spread = +0.47% (+47bps); 4-week trend up (steepening): Sep 3 spread ~+42bps → Oct 5 +47bps = +5bps steepening over 30 days; status supportive (both positive AND steepening on 4-week basis); yield curve steepening driven by 2Y falling faster than 10Y as Fed hold expectations rose sharply after the September NFP miss (+29K); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are the next major yield curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,743,031M ($6.74T) for week ending September 30, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released October 1 (most recent; next H.4.1 release October 8 for week ending October 7); 4-week trend flat: Sep 2 $6,737,204M → Sep 30 $6,743,031M = +$5.8B marginal expansion within flat threshold on a $6.74T balance sheet; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no QT acceleration); weak September NFP (+29K) raises probability of a Fed hold at October 27–28 FOMC, supportive for balance sheet stability.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately 0.0091% per 8h as of early October 2026 (~10% annualized per CoinGlass/CoinDesk), up from ~3% annualized in late September; open interest rose to 653,000 BTC ($56.2B) from 626,000 BTC on Sep 30 (CoinDesk Oct 2), signaling growing bullish leverage as BTC crossed $86,500; 4-week trend up: rose from ~3% annualized (Sep early) to ~10% annualized (Oct early); status supportive (0.0091% per 8h is well below the 0.04% overheating threshold — confirmatory of spot-driven accumulation, not leveraged speculation); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are next potential funding regime catalysts.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B as of early October 2026 (coinlaw.io/CoinGecko data, Oct 4–6); total crypto market cap ~$2.892T (down slightly from $2.92T on Oct 5); BTC.D 58.9%; stablecoin dominance ~10.5% (308/2892); 30-day trend flat: ~10.4% (Sep 5) → 10.5% (Oct 6) = +0.1pp change within flat threshold; status neutral (not falling on 30-day basis = not supportive; TOTAL essentially flat rather than rising = headwind condition not met); USDT and USDC hold ~83% of stablecoin market; ~$308B in sidelined capital available to deploy if macro improves; October 14 CPI is the next catalyst for stablecoin inflow/outflow dynamics.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes (September 15–16, 2026 Meeting)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the September 15–16 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET — the meeting at which the Fed raised the fed funds rate 25bps to 3.75%–4.00%; minutes will reveal committee debate on further tightening pace, any dissents, and how members framed the balance between inflation (ISM Prices 77.9%, CPI ~3.5% YoY) and employment risks; critical to parse for October hold signals given the subsequent September NFP miss (+29K); market is pricing high probability of a hold at October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 4, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 4, 2026 — first claims reading fully capturing early-October labor conditions post the September NFP shock (+29K); prior weeks approximately 206K; consecutive claims above 225K would reinforce Fed hold expectations for October 27–28 and signal the NFP miss is a trend rather than a one-off; released the day after FOMC Minutes, providing a real-time follow-up to the September labor narrative.

upcoming.title: Fed Balance Sheet H.4.1 (week ended October 7, 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve H.4.1 release at 4:30 PM ET — weekly update to WALCL covering the week ending October 7, 2026; prior reading $6,743,031M ($6.74T, week ending Sep 30); this release will show whether the marginal expansion of the past 4 weeks continues or reverses; a shift toward contraction here, combined with rising overnight rates, would flip balance sheet status from supportive to headwind.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (October 2026 Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary reading for October 2026 at 10:00 AM ET; September final was ~69.1; provides early read on consumer confidence heading into Q4 — a key forward indicator for retail sales and consumption; with DXY at 102.17, real yields at 2.88%, and the September NFP shock (+29K) fresh, a weak print below 65 would reinforce risk-off tone; the 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations sub-components are closely watched by the Fed for second-round effects given ISM Prices at 77.9%.
